method: Case-insensitive ASCII word-boundary exact headword scan of all 1000 example sentences; normalized duplicate-example grouping. Heuristic signals, not grammar failures or CEFR approvals.
source_limitations: Publisher dictionary morphology and exact-sense observations do not constitute independent human English, Myanmar, CEFR, example or pronunciation approval. Cambridge grammar indexed search results returned direct HTTP 403 and are not counted as directly opened sources. No listening, physical iPhone QA or production deployment.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm.

publisher_evidence.summary: Oxford lists hand as a countable body-part noun and illustrates plural hands; plural is not a missing headword.

records.editorial_risk: The A1 hand example uses hands, which is valid plural grammar. Do not flag as an absent word or replace a natural plural example merely to satisfy literal-string matching.
records.independent_reviewer_task: Human-independent reviewer must verify original English, fluent Myanmar, grammar, exact sense, CEFR source alignment and audio before any signoff.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: To succeed in doing something difficult.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: အခက်အခဲရှိသော်လည်း အောင်မြင်စွာ လုပ်နိုင်သည်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: We managed to finish the work before the deadline.

publisher_evidence.summary: Oxford explicitly lists managed as the past form and manage to do as the successful-completion construction.

records.editorial_risk: B2 manage means succeed in doing something difficult, not manage a team. The draft managed to finish construction matches the intended sense; confirm the Myanmar translation reflects successful completion.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: To damage something so badly that it no longer exists or works.

shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: The fire destroyed the old warehouse.

publisher_evidence.summary: Oxford lists destroyed as the past form and describes severe damage or loss of function.

records.editorial_risk: The B2 destroyed example is a valid past form, not a headword omission; check whether warehouse destruction is presented as physical destruction rather than a separate figurative sense.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: To take hold of something suddenly or quickly.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: အလျင်အမြန်ဆုပ်ကိုင်သည်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: She grabbed her bag and ran outside.

publisher_evidence.summary: Oxford explicitly lists grabbed as the past form and the sudden physical-taking sense.

records.editorial_risk: The B2 grabbed her bag example illustrates a sudden physical action; preserve consonant doubling in British spelling and distinguish this from grab an opportunity or a quick meal.
